item.title: Inuwa seeks common Northern policy framework to tackle out-of-school children
item.description: Advocates unified regional agenda, investment in agriculture, agro-allied industries to combat poverty, insecurity Sultan applauds Gombe governor’s Almajiri education reforms By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Gombe State Governor and Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has called for a common policy framework and unified regional agenda to sustain education reforms, tackle the growing number of out-of-school children and accelerate human capital development across Northern Nigeria. The governor said addressing the region’s educational challenges required a coordinated approach that went beyond school enrolment to include poverty reduction, improved security, economic empowerment and the creation of sustainable livelihood opportunities for the growing population. Yahaya made the call at the 2026 Biennial Lecture and Awards Ceremony of the Barewa Old Boys Association (BOBA), held in Gombe, with the theme, “The Scourge of Out-of-School Children and the Implications for National Security.” Describing the theme as timely and critical to the future of Northern Nigeria, the governor warned that the increasing number of children outside the formal education system posed serious threats to social stability, economic productivity and national security. He observed that educational exclusion perpetuated poverty, widened inequality and exposed vulnerable children and young people to criminal exploitation, radicalisation and other antisocial tendencies. Yahaya recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2019, Gombe State had more than 500,000 out-of-school children, explaining that sustained interventions by his government had brought approximately 350,000 of them back into the classroom. He attributed the achievement to the declaration of a state of emergency in the education sector, construction of mega schools with expanded learning capacities, recruitment of more than 1,000 qualified teachers and establishment of Almajiri Integrated Learning Centres, among other initiatives. Drawing from the state’s experience, the governor urged Northern states to move away from fragmented interventions and embrace a common regional framework that would identify successful educational models, encourage their adoption across state boundaries and guarantee continuity. He proposed that the Northern States Governors’ Forum should provide the institutional platform for harmonising educational policies, coordinating priorities and strengthening collaboration among the 19 Northern states. According to him, a unified Northern Agenda would ensure that successful programmes initiated by successive administrations were sustained, while promoting the sharing of resources, expertise and best practices for regional development. He maintained that the magnitude of the challenges confronting Northern Nigeria required collective responsibility, stressing that no single state could effectively address the problem of out-of-school children in isolation

item.title: Ebonyi govt lifts suspension on Ambertone as Ishiagu Community buries slain youths
item.description: By Chiamaka Ekwuwe The Ebonyi State Government has lifted the temporary suspension on mining operations at the Ambertone Logistics Limited facility, operated by Zotmann Mining Limited, in Ihetutu community, Ishiagu, Ivo Local Government Area, following consultations with relevant stakeholders and the burial of two youths who died in a shooting incident in the area. The resumption of operations on Wednesday followed days of engagements involving the state government, representatives of the mining company, bereaved families and community stakeholders aimed at restoring peace and normalcy. The development comes after the deaths of Chibuike Elema, 18, and Obinna Gideon Akandu, 20, in a shooting incident reportedly involving a military officer on Sunday, October 18, 2026. The precise circumstances surrounding the incident, including the events leading to the shooting and the responsibility of the personnel involved, remain subject to clarification by the appropriate authorities. Available accounts indicate that the incident occurred approximately three kilometres from the company’s operational facility, reportedly near another mining concession. Following the incident, tensions reportedly escalated in the community, with some youths allegedly attacking the mining company’s facility, resulting in damage to vehicles, equipment, offices and other property. In response to the developments and concerns over public safety, the Ebonyi State Government ordered a temporary suspension of mining activities at the affected facility to prevent further escalation and facilitate peace-building efforts. Following consultations and reconciliation engagements, the government subsequently announced the lifting of the suspension, allowing operations to resume. Ambertone, Zotmann Clarify Company Identity The incident also generated conflicting reports concerning the identity of the mining company operating the affected facility. While some initial reports associated the incident with Palladium Mining Company, subsequent clarification from company representatives identified Ambertone Logistics Limited as the company whose facility was affected by the unrest. Representatives further clarified that Palladium Mining Company operates a separate facility in the community and is distinct from Ambertone Logistics Limited and its operational partner, Zotmann Mining Limited. The clarification was issued to address confusion arising from reports that appeared to have linked Palladium Mining Company to the incident. Representatives of Ambertone and Zotmann also stated that neither company authorised the shooting, maintaining that the incident occurred outside their operational premises. The circumstances surrounding the shooting and any possible responsibility of individuals involved remain separate matters requiring appropriate investigation. item.title: Yoruba started home video, not Nollywood — Osuofia
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor, Nkem Owoh, popularly known as Osuofia, has clarified his position on the origins of Nigeria’s home-video industry, insisting that Yoruba filmmakers pioneered home-video productions but did not start Nollywood. Owoh made the clarification during an appearance on Curiosity Made Me Ask, hosted by comedian and content creator Adebayo Abidemi, popularly known as Bae U. The interview, published on the host’s YouTube channel on Saturday, featured the actor responding to a question about reports that he had claimed Yoruba people, rather than the Igbo, started Nollywood. The clarification comes amid an ongoing debate over the contributions of different ethnic groups to the development of Nigeria’s film industry. The debate gained fresh attention in August 2026 when late veteran actor Francis Duru argued that the Igbo built Nollywood but that Yoruba filmmakers had become more dominant because of their ability to organise and promote their productions. Duru, who died in October, had attributed much of the growth of the modern home-video industry in the 1990s and early 2000s to Igbo entrepreneurs. Reacting to the reported interpretation of his earlier comments, Owoh said it was inaccurate to suggest that he claimed Yoruba people started Nollywood, explaining that the name did not exist when filmmakers began producing movies. “First of all, you have given me this wrong accusation that I said, Yoruba started Nollywood. No. Yoruba started this film on… when did Nollywood come out? When we started the thing, there was no Nollywood as a name. “We sat together and we’re banding, you know, ideas and all that, how the thing is going to come to fruition. And eventually, we chose Nollywood,” he said. The actor, however, credited Yoruba filmmakers with popularising home-video productions in Nigeria, specifically mentioning veteran filmmaker Hubert Ogunde and Adebayo Papa as among those whose works he admired. “So, Yoruba started the thing. They made the thing very popular home video and all that. Yes, they did. And I’ve said it several. Okay. Ogunde and Adebayo Papa. These are the people I love to watch their thing,” he said. When the interviewer jokingly suggested that Ogunde was Igbo, Owoh disagreed, insisting that the late filmmaker was Yoruba. “Ogunde is not Igbo. I’m telling you that Yoruba started it. When Ogunde was out, I don’t think there was any Igbo man who was that popular in that,” he added. He further emphasised the distinction between the origins of home-video productions and Nollywood, stating: “The Yoruba did not start Nollywood. They started Home video.” Historical accounts of Nigerian cinema trace the development of Yoruba filmmaking to travelling theatre groups led by figures such as Hubert Ogunde and Duro Ladipo, whose stage productions evolved into film and video productions decades before the commercial home-video boom of the 1990s. item.title: Messi wins second consecutive MLS Golden Boot after scoring 26 goals
item.description: Inter Miami’s Lionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday after the defending champions took second place in the Eastern Conference with a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season. The Argentine superstar did not score but set up the first two goals at Miami’s Nu Stadium, both from corners, to help procure his club a home-field advantage for the first two playoff rounds. Messi’s 26 goals this season were enough to make him the first back-to-back MLS Golden Boot award winner. Petar Musa of Dallas was second on 22, not scoring in his club’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado. Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada’s brace soon after the break sparked a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko’s late strike. Runaway overall leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record for a season with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. At 23-3 with eight drawn, Nashville won the East and broke the mark of 74 points set by Miami in 2024. Miami finished second in the East on 60 points as third-place New England failed to take advantage of Inter’s draw with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando to end on 58. Messi’s men will face Columbus to begin the MLS playoffs. Other East matchups send New England against Philadelphia, Charlotte against Chicago and top seed Nashville against the wild-card winner, Orlando or Cincinnati. Columbus took advantage of the Cincinnati loss with a 4-3 victory at Chicago to finish seventh and avoid the wild card round. At Miami, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring. Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0. De Paul made it three before halftime, but Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors early and bagged a second in the 55th minute. In the 90th, Aloko bagged the equalizer, responding first to the ball as Smalls’s shot ricocheted off the post. A visibly frustrated Messi hit the post in stoppage time before Aloko came inches from bagging an unlikely winner with a thunderous shot into the outside netting. – Seattle, Real advance – Western Conference champion Vancouver beat Canadian rivals Montreal 2-0 to finish second overall, giving the Whitecaps a home-field edge if they should face Inter Miami in a rematch of last year’s MLS Cup final. There were six teams fighting for the last three Western Conference playoff spots on “Decision Day” with every MLS squad on the pitch. Portland, Colorado and the Los Angeles Galaxy needed only to win to secure a playoff berth but only Portland did so, the Timbers winning 2-0 at Austin while Real Salt Lake beat the Galaxy 2-1 and Colorado fell at Dallas, which allowed Real into the post-season. Seattle claimed the other spot with a 2-1 home win over Los Angeles FC. Albert Rusnak scored in the first minute

item.title: Nigerian army restores official X account
item.description: The Nigerian Army has announced the full restoration of its official X account, @HQNigerianArmy, following an attempted cyber breach in August. The Army disclosed this in a post on its X handle on Sunday, saying the account was back under its exclusive official management. “This account is fully restored and back under the official management of the Nigerian Army. We appreciate your patience and understanding,” the post read. The restoration brings to an end a recovery process that began after the Army detected attempts to gain unauthorised access to the account on August 29, 2026, at about 5pm. The Army had subsequently worked to secure and recover the account following the incident. The post Nigerian army restores official X account appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Iran executes three men linked to anti-government protests
item.description: Iranian authorities have executed three men convicted of carrying out operations on behalf of Israel and the United States during anti-government protests in January, the country’s judiciary has announced. The death sentences against Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were carried out on Sunday after being upheld by the Supreme Court, the judiciary’s Mizan Online website reported. According to the report, the three men were found guilty of “participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups” during the protests. Mizan said the defendants threw Molotov cocktails and grenades, used bladed weapons and firearms, and set fire to public facilities in Karaj, a city west of Tehran. Other defendants in the case received prison sentences ranging from five to 10 years, the report added. The protest movement, which initially erupted in December over the rising cost of living, rapidly developed into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on January 8 and 9. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths during the unrest, blaming the violence on what they described as “terrorist acts” orchestrated by the United States and Israel. However, foreign-based non-governmental organisations have reported higher casualty figures and maintained that Iranian security forces fired on protesters. The number of executions in Iran has increased since the outbreak of the Middle East war, which was triggered in late February by US and Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic. item.title: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos forward, Oluebube Umejiaku, has explained how the team recovered from their opening defeat to Poland to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria began their campaign with a 2-1 loss to Poland, despite Umejiaku scoring as a substitute. However, the team bounced back, treating every subsequent fixture as a final on their way to winning the competition. The Flamingos defeated DPR Korea, Mexico and other opponents before overcoming Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to claim the trophy. Umejiaku, who started the tournament on the bench, became one of Nigeria’s standout performers, scoring crucial goals, including in the final, and winning the Golden Ball award as the tournament’s best player. Speaking to FIFA.com after Nigeria’s historic triumph, she said the players were determined to change their fortunes following the opening loss to Poland. “When we lost the first game against Poland, everybody said we needed to wake up because we didn’t come here to look at anybody’s face and we have to take every game as a final. We don’t downgrade anything; we play and we put all our best into every game.” Umejiaku also reflected on her journey from a substitute to one of the tournament’s most influential players, saying she remained hopeful of getting an opportunity to start. “Every time I went to training and every time I slept, I told God that I’m praying for all the people that are starting. But when I wanted to start, I just told God that it is my time,” she said. Another key contributor to Nigeria’s triumph was Awawu Bashiru, who initially had limited playing time under head coach Akeem Busari. Bashiru played just 77 minutes between the opening match and the quarter-final against Venezuela before earning her first start against Brazil. She scored twice in that encounter and also opened the scoring in the final against Japan. Reflecting on the team’s achievement, Bashiru credited their success to teamwork and the technical crew’s instructions. “I’m so happy, I’m so excited and I’m so grateful,” she said. “The teamwork, instruction and listening to our coaches is why we got the goals and why we won the final. We are history-makers. We made Nigeria, and the millions of people there, proud.” Busari, meanwhile, explained that his decisions to change the starting line-up were based on the players’ attitude, character and commitment rather than reputation. “No matter how good you are, I’m a coach that plays on character,” Busari said of making those key changes. “It’s all about mindset, attitude and merit; if they’re there, you get your playing time. If they’re not there, you’re waiting to come in. As a coach, we want everyone to wire up and play together.” Nigeria’s victory made the country the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first from the continent to claim a women’s FIFA tournament title. item.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Eisenkot to form new government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an election that left both his camp and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition short of a parliamentary majority. Herzog’s office announced on Saturday night that the president had informed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, of his intention to give him the mandate to form a government. The formal appointment is expected to take place at a ceremony at the president’s residence in Jerusalem on Sunday. “This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X following the announcement. The decision brings Eisenkot closer to replacing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, after the religious-nationalist coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s camp secured 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc won 48, leaving both short of the 61 seats required to form a government. During consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received endorsements from two Arab-majority political lists, whose support could prove crucial in the coalition-building process. However, uncertainty remains over whether Eisenkot’s bloc would accept a formal alliance with the Arab-led parties, particularly after more than three years of war in Gaza. Netanyahu has opposed any arrangement involving the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government with what he described as “terrorist supporters”. He has also called for a national unity government. Eisenkot, however, has indicated a willingness to work with Arab-led parties under certain conditions, including their acceptance that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled. He has also pledged to take action against extremist Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank accused of attacking Palestinians, describing the incidents as “Jewish terror” allegedly enabled by Netanyahu’s government. Despite his willingness to engage with Arab-led parties, Eisenkot opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He has also vowed to end Hamas’ rule in Gaza and destroy its military wing. Eisenkot served as Israel’s Chief of General Staff from 2015 to 2019 and commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah. During the conflict, he developed the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”, a military strategy advocating the use of overwhelming force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by Hezbollah. Under the Israeli constitutional process, Eisenkot has 28 days to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers and form a government. Herzog can grant him an additional 14 days if he fails to meet the deadline. If Eisenkot cannot secure a parliamentary majority within the allotted period, the president may offer the mandate to another candidate. Failure by any candidate to form a government

item.title: WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) has renewed its push for greater participation of women in business and leadership, identifying mentorship, visibility and empowerment as key tools for helping women access opportunities and advance their careers. The Executive Head of WIMBIZ, Omowunmi Akingbohungbe, said the organisation was committed to inspiring and empowering women to attain leadership positions while equipping them to become entrepreneurs. Speaking during an interview at the organisation’s 25th annual conference in Lagos, Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ connects experienced and accomplished women with emerging leaders to guide them through the challenges of building careers and businesses. “We’re big on mentoring. We connect mentors, accomplished and experienced women with rising leaders so they can handhold them and show them the path so they’re not reinventing the wheel,” she said. She also stressed the importance of visibility, noting that women needed to make their abilities known, develop confidence and put themselves forward for leadership opportunities. According to her, many women often hold back from applying for leadership positions because they feel they are not qualified, whereas men are more likely to take the chance. “Most times women will think I’m not qualified and all of that, but men would apply. And we also have the potential,” she said. Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ was therefore working to ensure women recognise their capabilities and have the confidence to pursue opportunities in business and public service. “At WIMBIZ, we train, mentor, empower women. We give women a right to be entrepreneurs at the same time,” she added. She described the organisation’s partnership with Autos, its official automobile partner for the annual conference, as part of its 25th anniversary celebrations. She said the partnership would also provide discounts to WIMBIZ members and free vehicle servicing for two years. The 25th annual conference was held under the theme, “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World.” The post WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FIFA U-17 WWC: Why we lost to Nigeria in final – Japan coach Shirai
item.description: Japan U-17 women’s national team coach, Sadayoshi Shirai, has praised Nigeria’s Flamingos following his side’s 2-1 defeat in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Shirai admitted that Nigeria’s speed and physical strength posed major problems for his players, particularly when the Flamingos managed to break through their defence. Nigeria secured the title through goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Awawu Bashiru, while Fuki Ito scored for Japan. Reacting after the encounter, Shirai acknowledged Nigeria’s superiority but maintained that his players gave their best throughout the final. “First of all, I have to say that Nigeria were a very strong team. We understood their strengths, but there were moments when they managed to get in behind our defence. Even so, I think our players fought incredibly hard until the very end, doing everything they could to cope with Nigeria’s speed and physical power. I also believe that if we had managed to score earlier, we might have had a better chance of winning the match. I want them [Japan’s players] to be proud of themselves. The way they fought until the very end of this World Cup will have inspired many people, and I hope they can take confidence from that,” Shirai said. Japan reached the final after defeating DPR Korea in the semi-finals, while Nigeria booked their place in the title decider with a victory over Brazil. The Flamingos eventually defeated Japan to claim the U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy, marking a historic achievement for Nigerian women’s football. item.title: INEC to meet over Atiku’s 2027 ADC ticket
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will meet next week to consider the implications of the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), including the emergence of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The commission said it would not take a position on the party’s leadership crisis until it obtained and examined the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment. The Federal High Court in Abuja had, on Thursday, nullified the Mark-led caretaker committee and invalidated decisions taken under its leadership, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Sunday, INEC National Commissioner and Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, said the commission would not rely on media reports to determine the court’s position. “We can’t take a position until we see the judgment ourselves. We have to get the Certified True Copy because we don’t take decisions or reports of what the court said based on reports because the reports could be wrong,” he said. Haruna added that the commission would deliberate on the matter at its meeting next week. “Well, this one is very straightforward. Even then, we are all here till next week when the commission meets. We will have to meet over it,” he said. He also said INEC would comply with any further court order arising from an appeal by the Mark-led faction. “Obviously, if the David Mark faction should appeal, which I am sure they will, and they get an injunction for stay of execution, obviously, we’ll have to obey that judgment,” he added. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, had on Thursday nullified the leadership of the Mark-led caretaker committee, ruling that its emergence contravened the ADC constitution, relevant provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution. The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by a former ADC Deputy National Chairman (North-East), Nafiu Bala Gombe, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the caretaker committee assumed control of the party. Gombe argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was constitutionally entitled to take over its leadership. He consequently asked the court to invalidate the actions of the Mark-led leadership and restrain Mark and former Minister of Interior, Rauf Aregbesola, from parading themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary of the party, respectively. In its ruling, the court nullified the process through which the caretaker committee emerged and the party conducted its presidential primary that produced Atiku as its flag bearer for the 2027 elections. item.title: U-17 WWC: Full list of award winners
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos emerged as the champions of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on Saturday in Morocco. The victory saw Nigeria secure the title , with Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scoring to seal the win for the Flamingos. Japan’s Fuki Ito found the back of the net, but her effort was insufficient to prevent the Japanese side from losing the final. Umejiaku’s impressive performances throughout the competition earned her the Golden Ball award, recognising her as the tournament’s best player. Meanwhile, United States forward Maddie DiMaria won the Golden Boot after finishing as the tournament’s highest scorer with 12 goals. DPR Korea’s Kim Son-gyong received the Golden Glove award for the best goalkeeper, while Japan was presented with the FIFA Fair Play Trophy. Below is the full list of award winners at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: Golden Ball: Oluebube Umejiaku (Nigeria) Silver Ball: Yu Jong-hyang (DPR Korea) Bronze Ball: Fuki Ito (Japan) Golden Boot: Maddie DiMaria (USA) Silver Boot: Yu Jong-hyang (DPR Korea) Golden Glove: Kim Son-gyong (DPR Korea) FIFA Fair Play Trophy: Japan Vanguard News The post U-17 WWC: Full list of award winners appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerians debate how much money is enough for Detty December
item.description: Nigerians have taken to social media to debate how much money is enough to enjoy Detty December, with proposed budgets ranging from ₦50,000 to ₦15 million. The discussion began after financial services company Cowrywise asked Nigerians how much they considered a reasonable budget for the festive season in a post on X. The question generated different reactions, reflecting varying expectations and spending plans for the December festivities. While some users suggested modest amounts, others indicated that enjoying the season could require millions of naira. One X user, Ernest Onah, said ₦50,000 would be enough for him, prompting Cowrywise to question whether he planned to stay indoors throughout the festivities. How much money is a reasonable budget for Detty December? — Cowrywise (@cowrywise) November 4, 2026 Another user, Farouk Umar, proposed a budget of ₦1 million, while Philip Stanislaus suggested ₦500,000 and was asked to explain how he arrived at the figure. At the higher end, another respondent, identified as Great~MUHD, suggested ₦15 million as a reasonable amount for Detty December. However, some users appeared less interested in spending money on the festivities. One respondent, VictorBen, jokingly said he would rather spend ₦3 million buying a MacBook and sleeping throughout December. Detty December has become a popular expression for Nigeria’s end-of-year entertainment season, characterised by concerts, nightlife, parties, travel, social gatherings and other festive activities. The period, particularly in Lagos, attracts Nigerians in the diaspora and international visitors, while entertainment venues, hospitality businesses and event organisers often experience increased activity. However, the latest debate highlights the different financial expectations surrounding the season, as Nigerians weigh the cost of entertainment and social activities against their personal budgets. item.title: Two waterway accidents kill police officer, woman in Bayelsa
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Two separate waterway accidents in Bayelsa State have claimed the lives of a serving police officer and a female passenger, the state Police Command has confirmed. The incidents occurred in Brass and Sagbama Local Government Areas, according to a statement issued on Saturday night by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed. The first accident involved a passenger boat that capsized along the Abedigbene waterways in Brass LGA on Thursday while travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa with eight persons on board, including a serving commissioner. The police said Maritime Union workers in Brass reported the incident, prompting a search-and-rescue operation by personnel of the Nigerian Navy’s Forward Operating Base (FOB) FORMOSO, in collaboration with local divers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community. Seven passengers were rescued, including the Bayelsa State Commissioner for Trade and Commerce, Dr Ebiere Jones, and an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. However, a serving police officer who was initially reported missing was subsequently confirmed dead. The second accident occurred at about 5:20 a.m. on Saturday, November 7, along the shoreline of Angalabiri Community in Sagbama LGA, when a tanker vessel belonging to Sterling Global Oil Ltd reportedly collided with canoes navigating close to the shoreline. According to the police, preliminary investigations indicated that the vessel struck and destroyed some of the canoes. One of the victims, identified as Mrs Victoria Abetnigo, an indigene of Angalabiri, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Ebedebiri General Hospital for treatment. She was, however, pronounced dead by the attending doctor. Her remains have been deposited at Ofoni Mortuary, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Reacting to the two tragedies, the Commissioner of Police, Bayelsa State Command, CP Ajao Saka Adewale, expressed sadness over the incidents and extended his condolences to the families, colleagues and loved ones of the deceased. The police commissioner particularly lamented the death of the serving police officer, praying for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased and strength for their families to bear the losses. He also commended the Nigerian Navy’s FOB FORMOSO, local divers, Maritime Union workers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community for their prompt intervention during the rescue operation. Adewale urged boat operators and commercial vessel owners to exercise caution and comply strictly with maritime safety regulations. He specifically called on vessel operators to maintain safe distances from shorelines and established canoe routes and avoid reckless navigation. He also advised passengers to wear life jackets throughout their journeys and urged all waterway users to prioritise safety and promptly report emergencies to the appropriate authorities. item.title: Peter Obi congratulates Flamingos on U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has congratulated the Nigeria U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Obi praised the players for their talent, resilience, hard work and dedication, saying their achievement had brought immense joy and pride to Nigerians. In a congratulatory message posted on his X handle on Saturday, the former Anambra State governor commended the team for representing the country proudly on the international stage. item.title: Rumbling in Yoruba land: There’s only one Afenifere despite alleged breakup plan – Secretary
item.description: • Says Adebanjo endorsed Peter Obi in 2023 without telling anybody • Explains how Fasoranti endorsed Tinubu for president despite supplanting his leadership By Dapo Akinrefon Chief Ademola Folarin, a lawyer, is the General Secretary of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere. Folarin, who is the Agbaakin Maiyegun of Ibadanland, in this interview, speaks on the leadership crisis in Afenifere, reconciliation in the group, and the decision of the Yoruba body to endorse President Bola Tinubu for 2027 among other issues. Excerpts: There have been issues in the polity ahead of 2027, parties have been trading accusations; there is mudslinging. Do you think this is healthy for our democracy? Look, adversarial politics is one of the hallmarks of democracy. You have to destroy one party in order for you to rise. It’s one of the pitfalls of democracy that we can’t avoid, which is why some people say democracy is not the best form of government. But we haven’t found a better one. I think we are just being dishonest. There is a better one, it’s not necessarily democratic. We can see it in China, we can see it in the Gulf states, a combination of constitutionalism and monarchy. In China, there is no monarchy, but they have a system of evolutionary leadership, and it is working. The trouble spots in the world are the democracies. Just look around you, everywhere you see a problem, it’s democratic. That’s because it has to be like that. If you want to see the downfall of someone to rise, you can’t have peace, you can’t have stability. The bastion of democracy, Europe and America, are on the decline. It’s consistent with the aims and objectives of the founding fathers of democracy. It was foreseen, but it was unavoidable. If you choose your leaders based purely on numbers, you cannot avoid obvious mistakes. In our country, with the presidential system, it is the same in America. We have simply imported a corrupt system here, presidential system. If you don’t have money, you can’t do anything. That’s what you have. Mudslinging, everything is part of it. Nigeria has practised the parliamentary system before. Now, it’s practising the presidential system. Which do you think Nigeria can adopt? Do you think it should jettison the two and have another system of government? It’s a no-brainer which one should prefer between the Westminster parliamentary system and the presidential system. The Westminster parliamentary system is far cheaper and far more representative. Why do I say so? If I want to be prime minister, I don’t need to do a national campaign or whatever. I go to Eti-Osa local government, campaign and win there. Once I win there and my party wins the majority of seats in parliament, I form government. But in presidential, I have to win the majority of votes in the entire country.
